summary: Keep face identity and shared edges visible while unfolding a solid.
objective: Show a cube net folding into a cube, with hinge edges and matching cut edges highlighted.
example_prompts: Show a cube net folding into a cube, with hinge edges and matching cut edges highlighted.

entities.name: Faces
entities.guidance: Use thin panels with labeled front/back and consistent edge lengths; render thickness only as a display offset.

entities.name: Hinges
entities.guidance: Place each pivot on the shared edge, with child faces inheriting upstream hinge motion.

entities.name: Cut edges
entities.guidance: Give matching seams the same ID and distinct endpoint markers; do not hide overlaps with transparency.

state_contract.model: Authored valid cube net, face adjacency and hinge spanning tree; zero-thickness mathematical panels.
state_contract.authority: One canonical model owns semantic values; derive geometry and labels from it. Keep presentation transforms separate.
actions: Select a face to trace its neighboring edges.

invariants: Hinge endpoint distances remain equal throughout motion.
Flat configuration has no interior face overlap; closed target has matching seam positions.
Do not claim every planar adjacency tree folds to the target solid.
motion_guidance: Compute transforms from rest pose and hinge angles, not cumulative rotations.
Check intermediate face intersections; endpoint correctness does not establish a collision-free folding path.
known_limits: Source demonstrates unfoldings, not the particular authored hinge path; that path requires geometric validation.
No sheet thickness, flexible material or fabrication allowance model.
Authored guidance; no scene runtime or visual verification has run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Polyhedron unfoldings can be presented as planar nets that assemble into their intended solids.
claims.scope: Existence illustrated by the cited cube and other examples; not a claim about every net.

source_refs.locator: Opening description and Real Models table
